findings.title: Password check can be bypassed when a backup code is submitted with a dummy totpCode
findings.body: The credentials authorize function skips password verification whenever credentials.totpCode is truthy. Because the new backup-code branch is taken when credentials.backupCode is present, an attacker who knows a valid backup code for a password-based CAL account can also send any non-empty totpCode and bypass the account password check. Password verification should be enforced for password-based accounts when using backup codes, not skipped merely because a totpCode field is present.

findings.title: Backup-code login is blocked for non-CAL identity providers
findings.body: In the credentials authorize function, the early checks for non-CAL users only treat credentials.totpCode as a valid second-factor presence. A Google/SAML user who has 2FA enabled and submits a backup code without a TOTP code hits the ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled error at line 113, and can also hit IncorrectEmailPassword at line 117. These checks need to account for credentials.backupCode as well, otherwise backup codes do not work for SSO/Google 2FA users.

findings.title: Lost access button is unavailable in the external TOTP login flow
findings.body: When totpEmail is present, which is the flow used after Google/SAML authentication when 2FA is enabled, the login page renders ExternalTotpFooter instead of TwoFactorFooter. ExternalTotpFooter only contains a Cancel button, while the Lost access button that switches to the backup-code input is only in TwoFactorFooter. As a result, users in the external 2FA flow cannot reach the backup-code form.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic and can allow reuse
findings.body: During backup-code login, the code decrypts the stored backup-code array, finds the matching index, then writes the modified array back in a separate update. Two concurrent login attempts using the same backup code can both read the array before either update commits, both pass validation, and both succeed. This violates the intended one-time-use property of backup codes.

findings.title: Dismissing the modal after 2FA is enabled can leave the UI stale
findings.body: After handleEnable succeeds, 2FA is already enabled server-side and the modal shows backup codes. The explicit Close button calls resetState and onEnable, but dismissing the dialog through onOpenChange, for example via Escape, backdrop click, or dialog close chrome, does not. In that case the parent settings UI is not notified that 2FA was enabled, and the component retains stale backup codes and secret state.

findings.title: resetState does not clear the TOTP form value or sensitive state
findings.body: resetState only clears password, error message, and step. It does not reset the react-hook-form totpCode value, clear backupCodes/secret/dataUri, or revoke backupCodesUrl. Because the component auto-submits whenever totpCode has length 6, a stale six-digit code from a previous enable attempt can be submitted automatically the next time the OTP step is opened.

findings.title: E2E coverage for backup-code authentication is missing and the enable test does not dismiss the backup-code screen
findings.body: The PR adds backup codes but the tests do not exercise logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code. In addition, the first enable-2FA test now stops after entering the TOTP while the new backup-codes dialog is open; it never clicks backup-codes-close, even though onEnable is only called from that close action. This means the test does not validate the new backup-code screen and may pass while the modal is still blocking the UI.

findings.title: Backup-code comparison is case-sensitive and does not trim input
findings.body: The backup-code check uses credentials.backupCode.replaceAll('-', '') and then performs a strict array lookup. Generated codes are hexadecimal, but users may enter uppercase characters, especially given the XXXXX-XXXXX placeholder, or accidental surrounding whitespace. Valid codes can therefore be rejected. The code should normalize input, for example trim and lowercase it, in both login and disable flows.

findings.title: Disable modal can reopen in the Lost access state after being closed
findings.body: The modal does not reset twoFactorLostAccess, or error state, when it is closed via cancel or dialog dismissal. If a user switches to the backup-code Lost access view and then closes the modal without disabling 2FA, reopening the modal can unexpectedly show the backup-code input instead of the TOTP input.
